findings.title: No duplicate $149 charge on 2026-09-14 - single authorization+capture retry, not two charges
findings.explanation: TX-9002 was an authorization (temporary hold) created 2026-09-14T10:02:11Z for $149 against INV-2609 that hit a gateway capture_timeout and was never captured (capture_status=not_captured); it was released 2026-09-18. TX-9001, created 19 seconds later (10:02:49Z) and explicitly linked to TX-9002, is the settlement that actually captured $149 against the same invoice. Per POL-B-AUTH v1, an authorization is not a charge, and a released authorization after capture timeout is expected gateway retry behavior, not a duplicate charge. Only one $149 payment was ever captured. The customer's billing view showing 'two $149 charges' reflects the auth+capture pair, not two settlements.

findings.title: Support agent S-22 improperly promised a refund before billing review
findings.explanation: POL-B-REF states refunds require billing-specialist approval and support agents may not promise a refund before billing review. In SUP-5601, agent S-22 told the customer a $149 refund would be processed within 5-7 business days, based on a mistaken 'duplicate charge' conclusion, without billing review. This commitment should not have been made and is now correctly being withheld per S-05's note in SUP-5602 pending full investigation. This finding is a process error, not a billing/ledger error - no refund is actually owed since no duplicate charge occurred.

findings.title: Deep Time Analytics add-on charge is legitimate
findings.explanation: SE-6 shows the deep_time_monthly add-on ($30) was added 2026-09-12 by U-2 (an admin seat) via the portal, correctly set to start at the next renewal (2026-09-14). POL-B-ADD confirms admins may add add-ons, and they start at next renewal, invoiced separately at full monthly price. TX-9003 shows exactly this: a $30 settlement on 2026-09-14 against a separate invoice (INV-2609-AO). The owner's claim of 'never added' is contradicted by the subscription event log showing admin U-2 (a seat the owner authorized) added it.

findings.title: July upgrade proration (INV-2607P, $59.60) correctly calculated
findings.explanation: Per POL-B-PRO, mid-cycle upgrade charges new_plan_price * remaining_days/period_days. Vault plan is $149/mo over a 30-day period; 12 remaining days of that cycle gives 149*12/30=$59.60, matching INV-2607P exactly. This matches SUP-5549's resolution (no credit due) from an earlier, separate review. No error here.

findings.title: Unapplied proration credit CR-778 ($19.60) not flagged to owner despite being aged >30 days with auto-apply disabled
findings.explanation: CR-778 ($19.60, proration_unused_time from the July upgrade) has been unapplied since 2026-07-02. auto_apply_credits was disabled 2026-05-02 (SE-4/SUP-5390), predating this credit, so it never auto-applied. POL-B-CRD requires that with auto-apply disabled, credits unapplied for more than 30 days must be flagged to the account owner (owner_notified=true). As of the most recent ticket activity (SUP-5602, opened 2026-09-16), CR-778 is over two months old and owner_notified is still false. This is a clear, actionable policy violation independent of the refund dispute, and should be remedied by notifying the owner and letting them instruct whether to apply or refund it.

corrections.prior_claim: Two $149 payments for INV-2609 appear as a duplicate charge; agent concluded 'duplicate charge' and promised a refund.
corrections.corrected_claim: Only one $149 payment (TX-9001) was ever captured for INV-2609. TX-9002 was an authorization that timed out and was never captured (released 2026-09-18) - standard gateway retry behavior per POL-B-AUTH, not a duplicate charge. No refund is owed for this item.

corrections.prior_claim: Owner states the Deep Time Analytics $30 charge was 'never added.'
corrections.corrected_claim: The add-on was added on 2026-09-12 by U-2, an admin seat on the account (SE-6), consistent with POL-B-ADD which permits admins to add add-ons. The charge is legitimate; the owner may not have been aware another seat holder added it, but it was correctly initiated and invoiced.

unresolved_questions: Should the account owner be informed that U-2 (admin) added the Deep Time Analytics add-on, in case this was unauthorized internally (a seat-permissions/communication issue rather than a billing error)?
Does S-22's improper refund promise in SUP-5601 require any formal retraction/communication to the customer, and who authorizes that customer-facing correction?
Should CR-778 be applied to a future invoice, refunded, or left on account - pending owner's instruction once notified per POL-B-CRD?
